- When sentiment drops to 0.00 or below for multiple consecutive days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias correction in next 5–7 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80) after a high, model overreacts — adjust forecast to align with recent low range.
- When sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., >0.70) but price declines, model may ignore sentiment — reduce forecast slope or add downward adjustment.
- If model forecasts a steady upward trend but true outcome shows volatility or sharp drops, reduce forecast slope or introduce volatility buffer.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from model’s first 5 days, re-evaluate baseline and adjust for sentiment-driven volatility.
- If sentiment history shows a sharp drop from high (e.g., 0.82 → 0.00), model often fails to anticipate sharp drop — reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.
- When model forecasts a flat or rising trend but true outcome shows a sharp drop in the middle of the horizon, adjust forecast to reflect early volatility or sentiment shift.
